rawSections.text: The MG-43 Machine Gun is unlocked by default.
General Call-in Time Standard 7.75 seconds Upgraded 4.75 seconds Uses Unlimited Cooldown Standard 480 seconds With Morale Augmentation 456 seconds

MG-43 MACHINE GUN Fire Rate 760 rpm Recoil 21.25 Horizontal Recoil 17.5 Vertical Recoil 25 Spread ↔[4.00] ↕[4.00] Sway 1 Ergonomics 15 Noise Medium (~48m) Capacity 175 Spare Magazines 3 Starting Magazines 2 Mags from Supply 2 Mags from Ammo Box 1 Attacks *MG-43 P Projectile MG-43 P Projectile Mass 11 g Initial Velocity 820 m/s Drag Factor 30% Gravity Factor 100% Penetration Slowdown 25% Damage Standard 90 Ballistic vs. Durable 23 Ballistic Penetration Direct Medium Slight Angle Medium Large Angle Medium Extreme Angle Very Light Special Effects Demolition Force 10 Stagger Force 20 Push Force 12

As a general-purpose machine gun, the MG-43's large magazine size and sustained Medium penetration damage makes it excel versus crowds of small- to medium-sized enemies. This makes it particularly effective versus the Illuminate, given the abundance of lightly armored, high health targets. The weapon has high recoil, encouraging the use of crouching or prone stances and firing in bursts. The weapon's fire rate can be toggled between 630, 760, and 900 rounds per minute. A lower fire rate reduces recoil and conserves ammunition at the cost of overall damage output. A higher fire rate maximizes damage output, but makes the weapon harder to control. The MG-43's poor ergonomics makes it difficult to track or swap between targets at close range. This can be alleviated by equipping armor with the Peak Physique or True Grit passive. Another drawback of the MG-43 is its stationary reload, which can leave Helldivers vulnerable. This is also alleviated by equipping armor with the True Grit passive. It can also be partly mitigated by reloading before the current magazine is empty, shortening the reload time by 0.7 seconds. The weapon's staged reload allows Helldivers to reposition, and then resume the process once safe.

The following Ship Modules affect the MG-43 Machine Gun: Department Ship Module Effect Patriotic Administration Center Donation Access License Support Weapons deploy with the maximum number of carriable magazines. Streamlined Request Process Decreases Support Weapon stratagem cooldown by 10%. Superior Packing Methodology Resupply stratagem boxes refill Support Weapons with the maximum number of carriable magazines. Payroll Management System Reduces reload time for all support weapons by 10%. Bridge Morale Augmentation Reduces cooldown time for all Stratagems by 5%. Engineering Bay Streamlined Launch Process All Support Weapon stratagems launch immediately once called in, reducing overall deployment time.

rawSections.text: The Stalwart is unlocked at the Patriotic Administration Center for 3500 Requisition Slips at Level 1. The Stalwart can also be found at some Minor Places of Interest.
General Call-in Time Standard 7.75 seconds Upgraded 4.75 seconds Uses Unlimited Cooldown Standard 480 seconds With Morale Augmentation 456 seconds

M-105 STALWART Fire Rate 850 rpm Recoil 15 Horizontal Recoil 12.5 Vertical Recoil 17.5 Spread ↔[6.00] ↕[6.00] Sway 1 Ergonomics 40 Noise Medium (~48m) Capacity 250 Spare Magazines 3 Starting Magazines 2 Mags from Supply 2 Mags from Ammo Box 1 Attacks *AR-23 P Projectile AR-23 P Projectile Mass 4.5 g Initial Velocity 900 m/s Drag Factor 30% Gravity Factor 100% Penetration Slowdown 25% Damage Standard 90 Ballistic vs. Durable 22 Ballistic Penetration Direct Light Slight Angle Light Large Angle Light Extreme Angle Unarmored Special Effects Demolition Force 10 Stagger Force 15 Push Force 10

As a side grade to the MG-43 Machine Gun, the M-105 Stalwart specializes in dealing with large crowds of unarmored and lightly armored targets. This makes it particularly effective against the Illuminate, given the abundance of lightly armored, high health targets. The Stalwart has several advantages as compared to heavier options like the MG-43 Machine Gun or MG-206 Heavy Machine Gun. It sports a much larger magazine with a reload that, while still lengthy, can be done on the move. It also has much more reserve ammunition. The weapon also has higher ergonomics and lower recoil, allowing more responsive and accurate fire on close range threats. The Stalwart's major drawback is that it possesses only Light armor penetration, proving less effective versus enemies with more armor. For this reason, primary and secondary weapons with Medium or greater armor penetration pair well with the Stalwart. To leverage the Stalwart against targets of medium size or larger, Helldivers will typically have to aim for weak points such as Hive Guard bodies or legs, Devastator heads, Charger butts, and Hulk heatsinks. The weapon's fire rate can be toggled between 700, 850, and 1,150 rounds per minute. A lower fire rate can be utilized to conserve ammunition when targeting distant enemies or small weakpoints. A higher fire rate maximizes damage output, best used when faced with crowds or large unarmored targets. The Stalwart is one of the few support weapons equipped with an underbarrel flashlight, convenient for night missions or Hive World underground areas.

The AMR can also be found in some Places of Interest, primarily in Pods and Cargo Containers, and can also be found near the missile silo on Launch ICBM, Evacuate High-Value Assets, or Rapid Acquisition missions.

The AMR is a long-range support weapon, boasting a powerful 10x scope zoom and Heavy armor-piercing rounds. Its high damage rounds excel at dispatching medium sized enemies with a single well-placed shot. Several medium & large enemies on all fronts, such as Alpha Commanders, Devastators, and Overseers can all be killed in a single shot to their weak spots. Hulks can also be killed with a single shot to the eye, however this only works at closer ranges. Beyond roughly 30m, a second shot is required. The scope can switch between 50m, 100m, and 200m zeros, enabling the Helldivers to engage enemies from a mid to long range. The AMR can be fired as fast as the trigger is pulled. This grants high damage potential, albeit with high recoil. Aiming down sights, crouching, laying prone or equipping armor that reduces recoil, (such as Engineering Kit and Fortified) can greatly mitigate recoil. This high firerate is useful when firing into the weakpoints of heavy enemies, downing or killing them outright at speeds quicker than other Heavy support weapons. Due to the AMR's low ergonomics stat and the high importance of placing shots accurately, Helldivers may get improved results in shot placement by equipping armor with the Peak Physique or True Grit perks, both of which grant improved ergonomics. The low magazine size and lack of area-of-effect damage render the AMR ill-suited for crowd control. Helldivers may cover this weakness by bringing reliable close-range weapons like the AR-23A Liberator Carbine or other stratagems like the AX/AR-23 "Guard Dog". Uniquely, the AMR does not offer a weapon reticle in third person, meaning that Helldivers must switch to ADS to accurately aim the rifle. Despite this, it can be possible to aim and fire at targets without using the scope, as shots will still fire towards the center of the screen. The Anti-Materiel Rifle can open shipping containers at Minor POIs without setting off nearby explosive containers. The Anti-Materiel Rifle can be used to support teammates with Anti-tank weapons by destroying enemy parts, such as Harvester shield generators or Factory Strider miniguns.

The EAT-17 is the first unlockable Support Weapon that is designed to penetrate Tank armor, allowing Helldivers to kill heavily-armored enemies from the front. Its low cooldown, two uses per call-in, and disposability make the EAT-17 stratagem highly flexible. It can be used as a supplement to a more regularly carried Support Weapon, only being called down upon encountering armored targets and structures. Conversely, Helldivers can call in EATs immediately when off cooldown, stockpiling several launchers for later use. Attacks with the Hellpod itself are a potent and economical option against enemy spawners (Bug Holes, Bile Titan Bug Holes, Fabricators), also able to be leveraged against heavies with careful timing or by sticking the Stratagem ball to them. The EAT can be safely used at close range, dealing the majority of its damage with its projectile and having a small explosion radius. This and the launcher's ability to be hip-fired are particularly useful when being closely pursued by heavy enemies like Chargers and Hulks. One disadvantage is its lengthy readying time each launcher requires before firing when equipped from the Hellpod or after being stowed. Another drawback is a vulnerability to Stratagem-disrupting effects such as Ion Storms, Stratagem Jammers or Scramblers, and Cognitive Disruptors. It also becomes completely unavailable after Super Destroyers leave. In terms of damage, the EAT occupies the middle tier compared to other anti-tank weapons. The FAF-14 Spear and GR-8 Recoilless Rifle inflict significantly more damage, making them more consistent against armored targets and able to destroy certain structures like Shrieker Nests or Spore Spewers in a single shot, while the EAT cannot. The LAS-99 Quasar Cannon deals the same damage per shot as the EAT. It must charge up before firing, and is stowed to cool off between shots, unlike the EAT which is discarded after use. The MLS-4X Commando and the EXO-45 Patriot Exosuit's mounted rocket pod both deal about half as much damage, requiring multiple shots to defeat armored enemies compared to the EAT, even when targeting weak spots.

The Recoilless Rifle has two firing modes: HEAT, or High-Explosive Anti-Tank mode fires a highly-damaging Anti-Tank II armor-penetrating projectile with a small, low damage, Medium armor-penetrating explosion. HE, or High-Explosive mode fires an Anti-Tank I armor-penetrating projectile with greatly reduced damage (750 vs 3,200) in exchange for a larger, more powerful Heavy armor-penetrating explosion, similar to a G-12 High Explosive grenade, albeit with a slightly larger inner radius (3.5m vs 2.5m) and greater stagger force (50 vs 30).

The GR-8 Recoilless Rifle is an Anti-Tank II armor-penetrating support weapon with damage second only to the FAF-14 Spear excellent for swiftly eliminating large, heavily-armored enemies. It is capable of killing the majority of armored enemies such as Chargers and Tanks in a single shot. Certain larger enemies, such as Bile Titans and Factory Striders, can survive the one shot if it does not strike a weakpoint. The stratagem Hellpod contains both the Recoilless Rifle weapon and the ammunition backpack. The weapon cannot be reloaded without the backpack. The weapon wielder can carry the backpack to perform a solo reload, and a teammate can either assist the wielder and/or carry a backpack of their own to perform a team reload. One of the weapon's weaknesses is its stationary reload, requiring Helldivers to kneel in place for several seconds, leaving them vulnerable to enemy attacks. This can be mitigated in several ways: The staged reload has four steps: opening the venturi nozzle, removing the expended shell, inserting the new shell, and closing the venturi nozzle. Helldivers can take advantage of this by interrupting the process when under pressure, and resuming it once safe, retaining reload progress up until the latest completed stage. The reload animation can be cancelled to expedite the process once the HUD icon changes from red to white after the new shell is inserted. Performing a team reload greatly reduces the reload time, but requires another Helldiver's assistance. The effective rate of fire while team reloading is approximately 38-40 round per minute. Searching Minor Places of Interest for Ammo Boxes can help keep the weapon topped up without needing a Resupply. The Recoilless Rifle generates significant backblast when fired. While this will only knock down Helldivers rather than injure or kill them, it can still be a significant danger if a live grenade or stratagem ball is dropped as a result.

The FLAM-40 Flamethrower has a range of 20 meters, measured in first person view. Before firing, the pilot light must be lit by holding the fire button. It may be fired instantly at any time while the pilot light is active. The pilot light will extinguish automatically after a roughly 12-second period of disuse. The pilot light will appear to visually extinguish roughly 2 seconds before it mechanically extinguishes. This excels in dealing with hordes of enemies due to the large 10-meter reaching Area of Effect damage it provides. Firing at the ground will create a pool of fire that continues to burn for several seconds. This can set Helldivers on fire too, so advancing while firing is not advised. Diving directly backwards while shooting the Flamethrower can catch the Helldiver on fire, due to their legs passing in front of the jet. Both first-person and third-person views can do this. While the first-person view fires from higher up near a Helldiver's head instead of the hip, both can still easily catch their feet on fire. Its stream of fire deals continuous damage throughout its travel. Skewering a target lengthwise can greatly increase the effect. This weapon performs best on open ground. The flames are easily blocked by terrain or worse, bounced back at the Helldiver at short range. Unlike chambered weapons, reloading it always takes the same amount of time regardless of how spent the canister is. Conserving a small amount of fuel will not remove any steps from the reload process. Each canister contains enough fuel for 18.6 seconds of sustained fire, and fuel is not consumed between lighting the pilot light and firing.
[1.001.100] Re-introduced collision issues with fire particles that causes flamethrower weapons to deal less DPS than intended.

The following Ship Modules affect the FLAM-40 Flamethrower: Department Ship Module Effect Patriotic Administration Center Donation Access Licence Support Weapons deploy with the maximum number of carriable magazines. Streamlined Request Process Decreases Support Weapon stratagem cooldown by 10%. Superior Packing Methodology Resupply stratagem boxes refill Support Weapons with the maximum number of carriable magazines. Payroll Management System Reduces reload time for all support weapons by 10%. Bridge Enhanced Combustion Fire damage from Stratagems increased by 25%. Morale Augmentation Reduces cooldown time for all stratagems by 5%. Engineering Bay Streamlined Launch Process All Support Weapons launch immediately once called in, reducing overall deployment time.

The AC-8 Autocannon can fire heavy Armor-Piercing High-Explosive Tracer (APHET) shells or can switch to Flak shells for use against crowds and airborne enemies (eg. Gunships, Shriekers, Elevated Overseers, etc) The Autocannon has a 10-round internal magazine that is reloaded via 5-round stripper clips pulled from the backpack. Reloading while carrying the backpack causes the Helldiver to drop to one knee and remain immobile during the animation. Reloading a single clip takes 2 seconds, but reloading the entire magazine from empty takes about 5 seconds, due to the Helldiver needing to cycle the bolt. It is advised to never let the magazine run empty to avoid a longer reload time. If the magazine is empty, Helldivers may choose to only load half the magazine and cancel loading the other clip The Autocannon's wielder can carry the ammo backpack, but if a teammate assists in reloading and/or carries that backpack instead, Team Reloading is much faster. Ammo Boxes will add 2 clips to the backpack, and a Resupply box will add 5 (10 if Superior Packing Methodology has been unlocked). Like all explosive weaponry, Helldivers are advised to not fire at enemies at point-blank range. The explosion from the Autocannon's explosive rounds will kill the wielder. It is highly advised to crouch or go prone when possible to fire the weapon for reduced recoil. The Engineering Kit or Fortified armor passives can help with reducing the Autocannon's recoil. The Autocannon can be switched over to fire flak rounds, which are proximity-triggered projectiles that explode into shrapnel. They deal less direct damage and have lower armor penetration than the default APHET rounds, but deal more area damage with a larger explosion radius. They can be used against the underbelly of Dropships to eliminate most, if not all, of the lightly-armored Troopers and Commissars before they are deployed. They are also highly effective for clearing out Shriekers, thanks to the proximity trigger effect. When compared to APHET, Flak rounds have more damage potential when used against large unarmoured targets such as a Shrieker Nest, Spore Spewer or Fleshmob and unarmored weakspots such as the Impaler's face or a Charger's abdomen. Flak shells have a range safety that will prevent them from detonating too close to the user, and which allows them to be safely fired past nearby allies. Even with the range safety, caution is advised when firing flak shells at close range as shrapnel is liable to fly back toward the user and cause critical injuries or death.

The HMG is a bulkier alternative to the MG-43 Machine Gun, sporting a lower fire rate but higher damage and Heavy armor-penetrating ammunition. Heavy armor penetrating bullets deal full damage against Medium armor, making it effective against enemies such as Hive Guards, Bile Spewers, Devastators, and even Hulks. The HMG suffers from high recoil, poor handling, and a smaller magazine size relative to other machine guns. With an extremely low ergonomics value of 0 (the lowest of all weapons!), the HMG struggles to track targets that are small, fast, and/or at very close range. Helldivers are advised to focus on medium to large enemies from a distance. Ammo management is especially important for the HMG, as reloading its 100-round ammo drum takes 5.5 seconds. Reloading while a round is still in the chamber reduces the reload time by 1.6 seconds, or almost 30%. Certain Armor Passives pair particularly well with the Heavy Machine Gun. The Fortified and Engineering Kit passives substantially reduce recoil when in a steady position, and the Peak Physique passive greatly improves handling. With only two reserve ammo drums, the B-1 Supply Pack and Siege-Ready armor passive (which increases the number of reserve ammo drums to three) are each useful for keeping the weapon topped off. Supplies from Supply Packs and Resupplies always replenish both reserve drums, even without the Superior Packing Methodology upgrade. The True Grit passive from the Castellan’s Creed Legendary Warbond is also worth mentioning, as it boosts reload speed and ergonomics by a fair amount. Some Optional Objectives can be destroyed by the HMG, such as Anti-Air and Mortar Emplacements, Spore Spewers and Shrieker Nests.

The Commando's laser-guided function requires manual guiding via crosshair. This function can be turned off via the weapon wheel to dumb-fire mode for short-to-medium range engagements and the missile will behave like an unguided EAT-17 Expendable Anti-Tank rocket. You cannot save that setting, as you get a new launcher with each stratagem call down. Prior to Patch 1.006.001, the Commando missiles would remember the last painted point of space and hipfired launcher missiles would automatically redirect. However this is no longer the case, and missiles will only guide while the laser pointed is actively being used and aimed. Compared to the similarly disposable EAT-17 Expendable Anti-Tank stratagem: The Commando has a roughly 71.42% longer cooldown (120s vs. 70s). The Commando deals 45% less damage per shot (1,100 vs. 2,000) but deals 11% more total damage per support weapon (4,400 vs. 4,000). Two missiles from the Commando (2,200 damage) will be able to deal with anything a single EAT-17 rocket (2,000 damage) can handle. Additionally, Cannon Turrets and Tank turrets have 2,100 HP, giving the Commando a major edge over the EAT-17 for these units. The Commando's missiles have significantly slower velocity than other rockets. The FAF-14 Spear's ATGM has the same projectile velocity as the Commando's rockets. However, they experience no drop and thus can be fired from extreme distances. The Commando's rapid firing speed allows it to quickly respond to threats on the battlefield It is possible to easily destroy Automaton Fabricators from a distance with 2 shots from a Commando, though firing directly into their vents will destroy them in one shot. The Commando occupies an intermediate niche between weapons like the RS-422 Railgun and GR-8 Recoilless Rifle. While capable of killing many heavy enemies in a single shot, it must do so by aiming at their weakpoints. This is most notable against Automaton heavy units, whose weakpoints still take substantial time and ammo to destroy with ballistic weapons. It is also more appealing to destroy certain enemy parts or break armor, as the Commando can do this in one shot without wasting too much damage. This can be seen with Factory Strider cannon turrets, Hulk legs, or the armor on Chargers.

The following Ship Modules affect the MLS-4X Commando: Department Ship Module Effect Patriotic Administration Center Streamlined Request Process Decreases Support Weapon stratagem cooldown by 10%. Bridge Morale Augmentation Reduces cooldown time for all Stratagems by 5%. Engineering Bay Streamlined Launch Process All Support Weapons launch once called in, reducing overall deployment time.

The RL-77 has two firing modes: Flak and Cluster. Its default mode is Flak. Flak Mode uses a proximity fuse that detonates 0.2 s after the rocket detects a target or obstacle within 2 m. It has a 1.5 s lifetime fuse or maximum range of 375 m. The bomblets have random time fuses lasting no more than 0.7 s. The minimum safe distance is ~30 m from the center of the explosion cluster in Flak mode. The timed fuses of the bomblets mean it may not damage everything below if it disperses too high up. For example, if fired past a Factory Strider's main body, the Devastators at its feet may survive some of the blasts. Cluster Mode utilizes an impact fuse rocket with a 0.25 s lifetime and a maximum range of 62.5 m. The bomblets will detonate upon impact after dispersing. The rocket's Cluster mode minimum safe distance varies by its altitude when its fuse expires. The higher one aims, the larger the area saturated by bomblets. The maximum dispersion radius of a Cluster mode rocket on level ground is 60 meters if fired straight upwards. It should be noted that this does not disperse the bomblets sparsely enough to ensure safety for the Helldiver firing the rocket. Cluster mode is ideal for uses in somewhat close quarters, such as urban environments, as the rocket can be fired past enemies to explode on surfaces behind them, neutralizing them without having the rocket prematurely detonate in close proximity. As an added bonus in urban environments, engagements will rarely occur beyond 62 meters, so unless a specific circumstance arises in which Flak mode is needed, Cluster mode will be just as devastating, without the greater risk portrayed by Flak mode.

The RL-77 Airburst is notorious for causing casualties to Helldivers and enemies alike due to its very wide area of effect. However, when used responsibly, it can be highly effective at clearing hordes or patrols of light and medium enemies with a single rocket. Helldivers should account for travel time and projectile drop when aiming at distant enemies with Flak mode. In terms of ballistics, the RL-77 projectile behaves identically to that of the GR-8 Recoilless Rifle, and the two weapons share an identical sight. However, it is generally advised to aim slightly above the projected impact point with the RL-77; this way, the flak round can detonate above the target rather than in front of it. Using Cluster as the "default" firemode can be helpful in preventing accidents. The lack of a proximity fuse will prevent premature detonations on enemies that the user does not intend to shoot. However, the bomblets will only explode upon impact, meaning that they can fall further than intended and hit teammates. The relatively short range of the Cluster mode can be used to the user's advantage. With the aid of enemy pings or the radar, the RL-77's rocket can be shot so that it detonates above or behind enemies. This has the ability to kill enemy groups without needing line of sight of them, useful when fighting in Colonies or other low-vision environments. With its high explosive damage, the RL-77 is capable of killing some heavier targets in a single shot. This can be done by detonating the rocket next to or directly on a vulnerable Medium weakpoint. Chargers can be effectively dispatched by switching to Cluster mode, and aiming the rocket to land under them. This will either outright kill them, or send them into a bleedout state. Enemies like Bile Titans or Factory Striders, though technically vulnerable, have healthpools that are too large to effectively damage with the RL-77. The RL-77 is highly effective against Fleshmobs, easily able to kill one or multiple with a single shot. This is due to their low Unarmored protection more than offsetting their otherwise high HP. It is best to aim for their feet, or slightly in front of them, so they are hit with the greatest amount of clusters. Like the GR-8 Recoilless Rifle, the RL-77 has a backblast when fired, knocking down any unfortunate Helldivers standing behind the operator. Like other backpack weapons, the RL-77 has a lengthy reload that can be alleviated by an assisting Helldiver. The backpack on the assisting Helldiver can be obtrusive if firing in third-person, due to the rockets' length. Aiming down sights or using the "switch shoulder" keybind may make it easier to acquire targets. It is possible to shorten the reload of the ABRL up to 0.8 seconds by animation cancelling via weapon swapping as soon as the weapon shows as loaded in the bottom left of the HUD. The Flak mode is also triggered by friendly Civilians, SEAF Soldiers and both the Patriot and Emancipator Exosuits. The M-102 Gunner FRV and TD-220 Bastion MK XVI do not trigger the Flak rounds. Shooting the ABRL too close to the Tesla Tower (up to ~1x its height) will also cause the Flak round to explode. This used to occur to other sentries but has since been fixed.

The Spear cannot be dumb-fired, unlike other rocket launchers. The wielder must aim it at a target which is inside of the large white reticle, causing a small yellow triangle to appear. This triangle is centered on the target and turns green with an accompanying "click" sound when the Spear has successfully locked on, which takes one second. The Spear can then be fired to launch a seeking missile which does high damage. Locks cannot be attained past 300 meters.

The Spear only locks onto "large" targets (larger blip on the minimap) and non-SEAF structures. A list of valid targets can be found below this section. The Spear requires a clear line of sight to the target to successfully lock-on. Obstacles like foliage and fences can prevent locks, even if it looks like they shouldn't. This is most egregious with the Bulk Fabricator as its targeting point is very low to the ground relative to its height. The Spear can still attain locks through smoke and fog, making it useful at countering Spore Chargers. The missile's upwards trajectory may cause it to miss enemies at close range. Staying at least 30 meters away from the target is advised. If forced into close range, Helldivers can go prone to lower the missile's trajectory. Aiming downwards will lower it further. The reload animation can be cancelled as soon as the HUD shows that a missile has been loaded into the launcher. The Spear performs best in relatively flat and open biomes, where enemies can be attacked at farther distances. Sandy and moor biomes are good examples, while the trees in primordial and swamp biomes can block missiles. The buildings in urban environments can obscure sight lines. The missile's trajectory is affected by where the Helldiver aims. Aiming left and right can curve the missile to hit weakspots at an angle, while aiming above and below affects the vertical trajectory of the missile. Diving right before firing a missile imparts the Helldiver's momentum onto it for advanced trajectory manipulation. The Spear's higher demolition force allows it to destroy Bile Titan Bug Holes. The Spear is able to destroy a Dropship with a single hit to the fuselage, killing all of its occupants. This is also able to destroy Vox Engines and Factory Striders. Engine strikes are undesirable, as this will generally not guarantee the occupants' deaths. Helldivers should wait until the Dropship begins slowing down before firing to prevent misses. The Spear is able to lock onto Stalkers even while they are invisible. This can be used to find them if one is aware of their presence, but not their precise location. The Spear is an effective counter to Dragonroaches, as one missile is sufficient to destroy a wing or the abdomen. The Stingray and Dragonroach can outrun the Spear's missiles, causing them to expire and be wasted. Stingrays are vulnerable when preparing a strafing run. Available Targets[edit | edit source] The Spear can lock on to the following targets: Faction Enemies Terminid Horde Brood Commander (Alpha) Stalker (Predator) Charger (Behemoth, Spore, Rupture) Dragonroach Impaler Bile Titan (Spore Burst) Hive Lord Bug Hole (Bile Titan) Shrieker Nest Spore Spewer Automaton Legion Scout Strider (Reinforced) Gunship Hulks Tanks (Annihilator, Shredder, Barrager) War Strider Factory Strider Vox Engine Dropship (Parked) Cannon Turret Anti-Air Emplacement Bio-Processor Command Bunker Fabricator (Bulk) The Illuminate Crusher Fleshmob Harvester Gatekeeper Veracitor Stingray Leviathan Warp Ship (Grounded) Warp Gateway

The Railgun fires projectiles using a charge-based mechanic, and primarily has two firing modes, Safe and Unsafe. In Safe Mode, holding down the trigger builds up charge in the weapon and quickly readies a shot. While the charge is safely held at 60%, the player's movement is greatly reduced and releasing the trigger will immediately fire the projectile, dealing a high amount of damage. There is no inherent danger in holding a charge in Safe Mode besides the reduced movement speed, so the wielder may charge the weapon for as long as they desire. In Unsafe Mode, holding down the trigger will overcharge the weapon, increasing the projectile's damage the longer the trigger is held. As with Safe Mode, movement speed is reduced for as long as charge is building up, and releasing the trigger immediately fires the weapon. Charging the weapon in Unsafe Mode can increase the additional damage dealt by up to 150%, causing the projectile to inflict up to 2.5 times the damage it would have in Safe Mode. When charged above 90%, which is after 2.5 seconds, the standard damage has been increased from 600 to 1500, same as the durable damage which increases from 225 up to 562.5. If the charge meter reaches 100%, which is after 3 seconds, the weapon will explode and inflicting heavy explosive damage to the wielder. The charge meter is visible on the weapon itself when aiming in first-person mode.

The Railgun is a high-damage low-fire-rate weapon that inflicts extreme amounts of damage per shot but is limited by its slow fire rate and the danger of self-destruction in Unsafe Mode. With a total combat load of 21 rounds, it is important to avoid using it against weak and numerous enemies, instead targeting large, threatening targets. Helldivers are advised to take caution when choosing to fire the Railgun, as their movement speed will become reduced, making them vulnerable to enemy attacks. The Railgun must be reloaded after every single shot. Helldivers should immediately reload after firing to ensure it is always loaded. Charging the Railgun for three seconds will cause it to explode, destroying the weapon and dealing fatal damage to Helldivers. Wearing armor with the Fortified passive halves the damage of the weapon's self-destruct when overloading, rendering the explosion survivable. The Railgun emits a constant sound while charging, increasing in pitch as it gets closer to full charge. Additionally, there is a visible charging meter that will fill up from top to bottom and change in color from yellow, to orange, then red. The Railgun is best utilized against large, heavily armored targets with fatal weakpoints. Many larger enemies such as Hulks, War Striders, Alpha Commanders, and Chargers have weak points that can be destroyed in a single shot with Unsafe Mode. Automaton structures like the Anti-Air Emplacement, Mortar Emplacement and small Bunker Turrets can be taken out by a single overcharged shot. The Railgun is the only ballistic projectile weapon which can take out Automaton Fabricators quietly, doing so in five fully charged shots. Due to the high penetration of the Railgun, it is possible to take out the eye of the Hulk while shooting from behind it at a specific spot. The Railgun, uniquely, does not lose velocity when it hits an enemy. This allows its projectile to take advantage of the overpenetration system and deal more damage to grouped-up enemies.

Similar to the FAF-14 Spear, the W.A.S.P. is incapable of being dumb-fired, and must acquire lock-on against targets in order to attack them. However, unlike the Spear, the acquisition time is very short and the weapon is capable of locking on to most enemy types rather than only buildings and elite enemies. The weapon's default firing mode, Burst Mode, will fire up to seven missiles at the target. Quickly tapping the trigger will fire one missile, while holding down the trigger will continuously fire missiles until the weapon's magazine is depleted. The missiles will launch forward and in a random direction before re-orienting and homing in on the target. The weapon's Artillery Mode consumes the entire magazine, simultaneously firing all remaining missiles as single projectile that flies upward and then strikes the target from a terminal angle, creating an overhead airburst explosion similar to the Orbital Airburst Strike. The more missiles there are in the magazine, the more powerful the strike.

The W.A.S.P. Launcher specializes in engaging medium-sized enemies at mid to very long ranges while also possessing the capability to inflict moderate damage to heavy targets. With seven missiles per pod and five reserve pods carried in the backpack, the W.A.S.P. has a total combat load of 42 missiles. An additional missile can be stored in the weapon, allowing for eight to be fired at once. The W.A.S.P. is incapable of locking on to small enemies such as Voteless, Troopers and Scavengers. The W.A.S.P. is capable of locking onto enemies 300m away. Conversely, its missiles cannot properly track enemies that are too close to the user. If the locked on enemies leave the 300m range the missiles will continue to track the enemy they are shot at, similar to the Spear. Use cases for this feature is minor and typically only applies to far Automaton Gunships or fleeing Illuminate Stingrays The majority of the W.A.S.P.'s damage is concentrated within its explosion, with 3/4 of the total damage being Medium explosive damage. The physical projectiles are the only component that deals Anti-Tank II damage. As a result, the W.A.S.P. is particularly effective when fighting dense groups of medium enemies, killing several with only one or two missiles. Smaller nearby enemies will also often be killed, depending on the positioning of enemies. The random launch direction of the W.A.S.P.'s Burst Mode missiles makes the weapon significantly more inconsistent, as they may impact surrounding terrain or buildings while traveling to their target. Against smaller, faster targets, the missiles may completely miss. The W.A.S.P.'s relatively low Anti-Tank II damage component, randomized launch angles, and inability to aim at weakpoints makes it a poor choice to fight heavy enemies with. The user will typically be forced to expend a pod or more to dispatch such enemies if they cannot angle the rockets into a vulnerable area. The weapon's Artillery Mode is best-suited for scenarios where one medium or large enemy is surrounded by a crowd of smaller chaff units. However, the exact angle and position that the artillery missile decides to detonate at is highly variable. The high ammo cost, low armor penetration, and general inconsistency make this a highly situational option. Burst mode can do the same job if the user can spread out missiles to hit across an entire group. The W.A.S.P. suffers from poor ammo economy, with it carrying only five pods in its backpack and being easily capable of expending an entire pod in a second. The W.A.S.P. is most notable on the Illuminate front, featuring excellent breakpoints against all common enemies excluding Harvesters. The W.A.S.P. is also capable of targeting certain structures like Bug Holes, Shrieker Nests, or Mortar Emplacements.

Rather than using magazines of ammunition, the Laser Cannon builds up heat in its Internal Cooling Element while it is firing. If too much heat is built up in the ICE, it will burn out and render the weapon unable to fire until the heat sink is replaced via a reload. As long as it has not fully burnt out, the heat sink will slowly cool down automatically when not firing, even if a Primary or Secondary Weapon is currently being wielded; this effectively gives the weapon infinite ammo if it is fired judiciously. From a nearly maximum heat ICE, the weapon will require 15 seconds to fully cool down under standard conditions. Additionally, the beam from the Laser Cannon is capable of igniting targets, setting them on fire if the beam has been focused on them for a period of time. A burning target will take damage over time to its main body, but only if its armor level is not greater than the penetration power of the Laser Cannon. Finally, when firing the Laser Cannon for the first time after a period of inactivity, it requires a short "warm-up" period where the weapon has to be charged before discharging its beam.

Because of its beam nature, the Laser Cannon is very easy to aim, since gravity does not affect its beam. This makes it particularly strong against highly mobile enemies like Gunships, Shriekers and Elevated Overseers, as firing is as simple as placing the reticle on target and shooting. When firing, the color of the refracting light on the target will help indicate whether or not damage is being dealt. Blue light indicates that no damage is being done, while orange lights indicate dealing damage. It will emit a buzzing sound when its Internal Cooling Element reaches around 75% of its capacity as a warning that it is about to burn out. Like other heat-based weapons, the fully overheated reload process is faster than when partially spent becuase the ICE ejects itself hands-free at the moment it burns out. If committing to a manual reload, Helldivers may want to burn the ICE out completely first instead of doing a slower "tactical" reload. The Laser Cannon has a warmup period of 0.5 seconds before firing, it is advised that Helldivers try to bring the Laser Cannon out earlier and prime it before it is needed. The Laser Cannon's beam nature, Heavy armor penetration, potentially infinite ammo, and it’s great range gives it great flexibility. Generally, it is best used to destroy medium armored enemies such as Devastators and Bile Spewers, as it can easily punch through their armored areas and inflict full damage while also igniting them. Against Automatons, it is also capable of destroying Hulks and War Striders quickly by focusing on their red eye units. Most light enemies can be ignited by sweeping the beam across them in one to two passes, allowing it to efficiently deal with large groups. Outside of a few exceptional enemies than can't be set on fire, quickly and repeatedly igniting larger enemies with short bursts allows for steady, sustained damage on them while still staying mobile. Despite having low damage output for a support weapon, it can sustain this damage over time and also inflicts respectable durable damage from a considerable distance. Combined with its ease of aim, the Laser Cannon is capable of melting high durability weak points over time. Its armor penetration allows the Laser Cannon to deal damage to certain secondary objective structures such as Anti-Air and Mortar Emplacements, as well as Shrieker Nests and Spore Spewers. This can be handy for destroying objective buildings without having to call down and wait for a Hellbomb. The Laser Cannon can open shipping container doors and break fences, thanks to its 20 demo force.

Because of its ability to rapidly fire explosive projectiles, the GL-21 excels at inflicting area damage at close to medium range, decimating light or medium armored enemies and inflicting decent damage on heavily armored foes. Unlike the AC-8 Autocannon, the GL-21 inflicts no direct impact damage, dealing the vast majority through their explosion. As such, they are much more effective at dealing with crowds. Grenades have a pronounced arc and slow velocity which rapidly decelerates. This limits the GL-21's effective range for precision fire, though it remains potent at area suppression up to approximately 100 m. The LIFT-860 Hover Pack pairs very well with the GL-21, as it allows Helldivers to fire down upon attackers from relative safety. Grenades fired from the GL-21 have a safety fuse that prevents them from exploding too soon after firing, causing them to harmlessly bounce off objects and enemies at very close range. However, after ricocheting, the grenade can explode once it travels beyond this safety range and impacts the ground or nearby objects Like other explosive weapons, the GL-21 can destroy Bug Holes and Automaton Fabricators by shooting into their weak points.

A single shock of the Arc Thrower can take down swarms of small enemies, such as: Small Terminids such as Scavengers, Warriors, and Hunters, holding off hordes of bugs singlehandedly due to the arcing lightning. Against the Automatons, it will one-shot all Troopers and quickly kill groups of Devastators and Berserkers. Against the illuminate, it will hold off hordes of Voteless, stunning any it does not immediately kill. Thanks to the level 7 Penetration, the Arc Thrower is able to damage even very large enemies such as the Bile Titan. Many heavy-units such as Charger, Hulk, and Fleshmob can be stun-locked with rapid firing. The stun effect can prevent Harvesters from using primary attacks. How to increase chances of hitting the target: Get to the high ground. Shoot from above. Aim a bit above the target. Avoid shooting enemies moving from left to right, or from right to left from you. Avoid situations when there are barriers between you and the target. For example, piles of corpses, mines, or structures. The arc cannot be aimed at specific limbs. If you are facing an enemy (like a Warrior) head on, the arc will always hit the head. Attacking from the side will hit the body. Medium-sized Automatons can also be headshot if you are lucky. The initial arc travel requires 1 cubic meter of clearance in the path towards the target. Helldivers must maintain clearance from objects like fences and walls, otherwise the arc will be interrupted before reaching the target. Arcs have an initial firing angle of 3-degrees. Shooting the initial bolt from a harsh angle will not initiate arc-chaining (e.g., right atop of targets while hovering above with LIFT-860 Hover Pack). Each fired arc may chain 1 time (3 with Circuit Expansion). The damage degrades with each chain following the formula: 1 / (1 + Max Chain Count). Without Circuit Expansion, damage dealt will be 100% -> 50%. With Circuit Expansion, damage dealt will be 100% -> 75% -> 50% -> 25%. The chained arcs also have a maximum targeting angle of 60-degrees. And similar to real-life lightning-bolts, the arc-chain generally travels the "shortest and straightest" path rather than "zigzagging" between targets. In other words, one arc-chain will only clear one single line of targets in a row. The arcs will chain indiscriminately between targets, which includes Helldivers and Civilians. Clearing a crowd of mixed factions with an Arc Thrower is highly discouraged, as it can quickly lead to a Helldiver being labeled a traitor and bombarded by the Super Destroyer. Each arc may only select targets within 55 meters of its initial position. This range limit resets with each target hit. The truly infinite ammo of the Arc Thrower allows for a Helldiver to be very self-sufficient and removes the reliance on ammo pickups or Resupplies for support weapon ammunition. Combined with energy weapons, such as the LAS-5 Scythe or ARC-12 Blitzer, one can completely eliminate their reliance on ammo.

The following Ship Modules affect the ARC-3 Arc Thrower: Department Ship Module Effect Patriotic Administration Center Streamlined Request Process Decreases Support Weapon stratagem cooldown by 10%. Streamlined Launch Process All Support Weapons launch immediately once called in, reducing overall deployment time.

An Energy-Based Support Weapon, the Quasar Cannon fires a burst of energy that can penetrate heavy armor and inflict significant damage. Rather than immediately firing the weapon when the trigger is pressed, holding it down begins a charging cycle that requires 3.0 seconds to complete. While aiming and/or charging the weapon, the wielder's movement speed is significantly reduced. If the trigger is released before charging is complete, all built-up charge is immediately dissipated and the weapon must start the process over. However, if the weapon is allowed to complete charging, it will launch a high-velocity energy projectile which is not affected by gravity. After firing, the weapon immediately overheats and cannot be fired again for 15.0 seconds, which is affected by weather modifiers. The weapon will cool down regardless of its wielding status, whether it is being actively held, it is being carried on the player's back or on the ground.

With a damage value of 2000, the Quasar Cannon occupies the middle tier of anti-tank weapons, alongside the EAT-17 Expendable Anti-Tank. As an Energy-Based weapon, the Quasar Cannon has several unique quirks and advantages. The Quasar Cannon does not need to be reloaded, nor does it require an ammunition backpack, giving it effectively infinite ammo. Its infinite ammo supply makes the Quasar Cannon exceptionally useful for Commando Missions. The projectile travels more than five times faster than the GR-8 Recoilless Rifle's shell and is not affected by gravity. After firing, Helldivers can switch weapons to immediately return to fighting while the Quasar Cannon cools down. Along with unique advantages, the Quasar Cannon has some unique disadvantages as well. Due to its 3 second chargeup and 15 second recharge time, the Quasar Cannon is not equipped to deal with several enemies at one time. Helldivers are significantly slowed during the charging process, making them more vulnerable to incoming damage. If the trigger is released at any point during charging, the charge will immediately reset and must be started all over again.

Bridge Morale Augmentation Reduces cooldown time for all Stratagems by 5%. Engineering Bay Streamlined Launch Process All Support Weapons launch immediately once called in, reducing overall deployment time.

SG-88 BREAK-ACTION SHOTGUN Fire Rate 600 rpm Recoil 33.25 Horizontal Recoil 6.5 Vertical Recoil 60 Spread ↔[60.00] ↕[60.00] Sway 1 Ergonomics 65 Noise Large (~58m) Capacity 2 Spare Rounds 40 Starting Rounds 20 Rounds from Supply 20 Rounds from Ammo Box 10 Barrels x 2 Attacks *SG-88 P Projectile SG-88 P Projectile Pellets x 9 Mass 6 g Initial Velocity 385 m/s Drag Factor 50% Gravity Factor 100% Penetration Slowdown 25% Damage Standard 65 Ballistic vs. Durable 13 Ballistic Penetration Direct Light Slight Angle Light Large Angle Light Extreme Angle Unarmored Special Effects Demolition Force 10 Stagger Force 20 Push Force 20

The SG-88 is a double-barreled shotgun with incredibly tight shot spread, capable of accurate fire up to 50 meters away. The SG-88 has the tightest shot grouping at 60 mrads of all shotguns. Due to the limited capacity, it is not recommended that Helldivers engage large groups or heavily armored enemies with the SG-88. The SG-88 will often spawn with only 2 shells in the chamber, it is recommended that Helldivers find a nearby Ammo Box or call a Resupply if they intend on using the SG-88. The SG-88 is the third-highest damaging shotgun in the game, only the M90A Shotgun and the DBS-2 Double Freedom being more powerful. This damage makes it very effective against lightly armored, high-health enemies such as Alpha Commanders and Bile Spewers, capable of quickly destroying fatal parts without needing to reload. Helldivers can set the SG-88 to fire both barrels at once, providing a larger burst of damage in exchange for more frequent reloads. While reloading just one of its two shells, the second can still be fired at any time in the animation with zero delay, interrupting the partial reload in progress.

CQC-72 Specific[edit | edit source] The main feature of the Entrenchment Tool is excavation of soft ground material by holding down "AIM"-button and then "fire". This action consumes stamina akin to weaponized melee strikes. Helldivers do not stop digging upon running out of stamina. The digging-motion also applies melee damage which also can be aimed any direction. Most hard materials such as pavement in Cities cannot be dug through, nor some areas too close to a structure or an objective like an Escape Pod. However, a texture is applied over the dug spot. Compared to using explosives, excavating using the Entrenchment Tool is slower but more precise and does not use ammunition. Trenches and foxholes dug using the Entrenchment Tool are helpful for providing cover in otherwise open areas for Helldivers and their equipment alike. The A/M-12 Mortar Sentry and its variants benefit especially from being placed in a trench due to their indirect fire attack. This is a suitable melee weapon for killing Voteless due to its high damage and attack rate. Its standard attack pattern when not aiming consists of alternating diagonal swings, identical to the CQC-5 Combat Hatchet. Helldivers can swing the CQC-72 Entrenchment Tool 20 times before running out of stamina. This number is not affected by Stamina Regen value or the Stamina Enhancement Booster. Melee Weapons[edit | edit source] Melee weapons deal all of their damage to the first segment or "body part" of any given entity that they come into contact with. Additional segments of the same unit that the weapon passes through will be ignored. Wearing Armor with the Peak Physique or Rock Solid passive will increase melee damage by 40%, greatly increasing its lethality. Armor with the Reinforced Epaulettes passive will increase melee damage by 20%,. Melee weapons are able to hit multiple enemies with one swing. Attacking with a melee weapon drains stamina. Holding the attack button will allow you to continuously attack, even when stamina is empty.

The TX-41 Sterilizer functions similarly to the FLAM-40 Flamethrower. It spews out caustic gas that slows and confuses enemies. The Sterilizer has a range of 47 meters, measured in first person.[1] Gas expelled from the Sterilizer has a DPS and Durable DPS of 25, lingers for approximately 0.25 seconds in the air, and cannot stick to surfaces, unlike flames and napalm. Unlike the Flamethrower, the Sterilizer doesn't have a firing delay due to the lack of a pilot light. Enemies under the effect of the caustic gas are slowed by 25% and become confused, causing them to run into different directions while uncontrollably attacking anything nearby, potentially hitting their own allies. The Sterilizer's canisters contain enough gas for roughly 16 seconds of continuous spraying. With its low DPS and strong confusion effect, the Sterilizer is a purely crowd-controlling tool that is best used in short bursts - quickly spraying gas to inflict the effect, then engaging slowed and confused enemies with other weapons or stratagems. The Sterilizer's spray is affected by wind, which can cause gas to drift away from the point of aim or even back toward the operator. Wind direction can be estimated by observing Helldiver capes, rainfall, or environment objects like foliage and flags. Diving directly backwards while shooting the Sterilizer will deal damage to the Helldiver, due to their legs passing in front of the nozzle. This damage can be reduced by equipping armors with the Advanced Filtration passive.

rawSections.text: The One True Flag is unlocked from the 3rd page of the Masters of Ceremony Premium Warbond for 110 Medals.

CQC-1 ONE TRUE FLAG Recoil 6.25 Horizontal Recoil 2.5 Vertical Recoil 10 Spread ↔[10.00] ↕[10.00] Sway 1 Ergonomics 65 Noise No sound Stamina Cost 3% Attacks *CQC-1 ONE TRUE FLAG_dm Damage CQC-1 ONE TRUE FLAG_dm Damage Standard 200 Melee vs. Durable 100 Melee Penetration Direct Medium Slight Angle Unarmored Large Angle Unarmored Extreme Angle Unarmored Special Effects Status Stun Large Status Strength 5 Demolition Force 10 Stagger Force 35 Push Force 30

One True Flag Specific[edit | edit source] Much like the Stun Lance, the One True Flag thrusts forwards at a decent range which allows you to target specific enemy parts, such as the head, to deal critical damage. Like the Stun Lance, the thrust can only hit targets right in front the Helldiver, requiring more care taken if being surrounded by multiple targets. Like the Lance, the One True Flag has a stun on hit effect, contrary to a lack of any reference in description or visual appearance. This weapon pairs well with the SH-20 Ballistic Shield as its narrow area of attack is remediated by the protection the shield offers. Unlike with other melee weapons the Helldiver will not move the shield off to the side to strike. When the One True Flag is stowed on a Helldiver's back, it will often obstruct the bearers view in third person view, making it harder to see what the bearer is shooting at. Choosing to drop the One True Flag will instead plant the flag at the Helldiver's feet. This deals damage to enemies, allies or objects at the point of impact. In situation that the flag cannot be planted, it will instead remain in the player's hands. Planting the flag will attach it to any large enemy or object. This includes the FRV and Exosuits. The damage caused by the flag plant is affected by Peak Physique, Rock Solid and Reinforced Epaulettes passives. Planted or dropped flags do not attract the enemy and must be equipped to gain that effect. Holding the Inspect Weapon button will wave the flag. Helldivers can swing the CQC-1 25 times before running out of stamina. This number is not affected by Stamina Regen value or the Stamina Enhancement Booster. Bug: If the Helldiver plants the flag, picks it back up, and then uses the Warp pack before equipping the flag, it will visually disappear until equipped. Should the Helldiver die while the flag is invisible, it will not be possible to retrieve the flag. There is a separate glitch that can make the flag fall off your back; the trigger is unknown. Melee Weapons[edit | edit source] Melee weapons deal all of their damage to the first segment or "body part" of any given entity that they come into contact with. Additional segments of the same unit that the weapon passes through will be ignored. Wearing Armor with the Peak Physique or Rock Solid passive will increase melee damage by 40%, greatly increasing its lethality. Armor with the Reinforced Epaulettes passive will increase melee damage by 20%,. Melee weapons are able to hit multiple enemies with one thrust. Attacking with a melee weapon drains stamina. Holding the attack button will allow you to continuously attack, even when stamina is empty.

Bridge Morale Augmentation Reduces cooldown time for all stratagems by 5%. The De-Escalator has an arming distance of 4m, under which grenades will ricochet, and its arcs travel approximately 12 meters, which can prove lethal to its user. As a revolver, the De-Escalator uses the rounds reload mechanic, unlike the GL-21 Grenade Launcher which is belt-fed. This means reloads do not waste ammo, but take long periods of time. Therefore, users should reload as often as possible before enemy forces prove overwhelming. The De-Escalator fires 10 arcs with Heavy armor penetration, enabling it to kill and stun large groups of weaker enemies as well as heavy enemies such as Hulks or Bile Titans. The De-Escalator can kill Bile Titans in a single cylinder (6 grenades) to their forehead. Hulks can be killed with 1 precise shot to their head/visor. The De-Escalator can effectively kill Chargers by firing 9-10 grenades at the ground to bounce up and have the arcs strike their vulnerable underside. This will cause the Charger to bleed out and die in 10 seconds. Unlike the standard Grenade Launcher, the De-Escalator cannot destroy spawners such as Fabricators, Bug Holes or Grounded Warp Ships as it is Arc not Explosion damage. For the same reason, the De-Escalator does poorly at destroying Bile Spewer or Nursing Spewer sacs; aim for their heads instead, or use explosive weaponry.

The Epoch holds 4 magazines by default, each containing 3 shots, which must be reloaded while stationary. In turn, it has Heavy to Anti-Tank I armor penetration and high explosion damage centered in a small area. Like the RS-422 Railgun, the Epoch must be charged before it can fire, risking the death of the user and destruction of the weapon if that charge is held for too long. The armor penetration only scales up to Anti-Tank I armor penetration when overcharged; this state additionally grants the weapon +100% bonus projectile and +60% explosion damage. The following are recognizable indicators to know the fully charged state of the weapon: The charge meter that can be seen either under the sight in first-person or at the back of the gun in third-person. This meter enters the red zone when the gun is overcharged. The muzzle flash that occurs only when the weapon reaches its overcharged state. The rapid beeping noises that also occur to indicate to the Helldiver that the weapon is ready to fire. The pins visible on the barrel of the weapon will retract into the barrel Firing the fully-charged plasma bolt will also result in a visually larger explosion with a more powerful sound effect.

The explosion of the Epoch's overcharged projectile is largely cosmetic, as the actual damage radius is substantially smaller and is only marginally larger than the SG-8P Punisher Plasma or PLAS-101 Purifier. As such, while the Epoch is capable of easily killing dense groups of Heavy Devastators or Alpha Commanders, the weapon's limited ammo, charge time, and relatively small blast radius makes it less than ideal for large crowds or spread out enemies. The projectile the Epoch fires has a 0.6 second lifetime, meaning that it only has an approximate maximum range of 150m. Unlike similar support weapons like the GR-8 Recoilless Rifle or the LAS-99 Quasar Cannon, the Epoch is severely impacted by enemy part durability and Explosive Damage Resistance. The Epoch's projectile does half as much durable damage as it does standard damage, meaning that the Epoch can lose up to a quarter of its damage when shooting at an enemy body part that is 100% durable. Half of the Epoch's total damage is contained within its explosion, which means that enemies with high ExDR values like the Harvester will receive significantly less damage than they otherwise would. Conversely, enemies with body parts vulnerable to explosion damage will receive far more damage, as all of their parts caught in the blast will receive damage. The Epoch has a 2-stage reload; ejecting the canister and loading a new one. One can animation cancel the reload the moment the HUD magazine shows as white/loaded. In situations where you cannot afford to sit and fully reload your Epoch, a good method is to "reload" by first ejecting the canister, remove the threat at hand, then reload the Epoch somewhere safe. The Epoch's uncharged plasma bolts only have a demolition force of 10. This demolition force increases to 30 when fully-charged, making it capable of destroying structures like Bug Holes, the vents of Automaton Fabricators, or Cargo Containers. Pairing the Epoch with a B-1 Supply Pack can help to mitigate the extremely poor ammo economy of this weapon. Using the Siege-Ready armor perk grants an additional spare magazine, slightly alleviating its limited ammo economy. Due to the long charge-up time, pairing the Epoch with mobility-related backpacks like the LIFT-850 Jump Pack or shield packs like the SH-32 Shield Generator Pack may help you charge the weapon without being staggered. Notably, when used with the LIFT-850 Jump Pack, the Epoch can begin reloading while the Helldiver is still in the air. Like the MLS-4X Commando, the Epoch often takes two or more shots to kill heavy enemies if care is not taken to hit their weakpoints. The Epoch's explosion damage allows it to exploit enemies whose body parts are not fully explosion-immune, like those of Dragonroaches and Chargers. By aiming at the center of Dragonroaches or at the upper-back of Chargers, enough body parts can be hit by the explosion to either outright kill the enemy or send them into bleedout[1].

rawSections.text: The S-11 Speargun is unlocked on the 2nd page of the Dust Devils Premium Warbond for 85 Medals.
General Call-in Time Standard 7.75 seconds Upgraded 4.75 seconds Uses Unlimited Cooldown Standard 480 seconds With Morale Augmentation 456 seconds

S-11 SPEARGUN Fire Rate 60 rpm Recoil 15.75 Horizontal Recoil 6.5 Vertical Recoil 25 Spread ↔[0.10] ↕[0.10] Sway 1 Ergonomics 35 Noise Medium (~48m) Capacity 1 Spare Magazines 12 Starting Magazines 12 Mags from Supply 6 Mags from Ammo Box 3 Attacks *S-11 P Projectile **Gas status **Gas Confusion status **S-11 P E Explosion S-11 P Projectile Mass 100 g Initial Velocity 300 m/s Drag Factor 400% Gravity Factor 100% Lifetime 1.70000005 sec Penetration Slowdown 0% Explode After S-11_P_E Damage Standard 650 Ballistic vs. Durable 275 Ballistic Penetration Direct Anti-Tank I Slight Angle Anti-Tank I Large Angle Anti-Tank I Extreme Angle Anti-Tank I Special Effects Status Gas Status Strength 50 Second Status Gas_Confusion Status Strength 50 Demolition Force 30 Stagger Force 80 Push Force 35 Gas Status Status Duration 6 sec Damage Element Gas Standard 25 Gas vs. Durable 25 Gas Penetration Direct Anti-Tank II Slight Angle Anti-Tank II Large Angle Anti-Tank II Extreme Angle Unarmored Special Effects Demolition Force 0 Stagger Force 0 Push Force 0 Gas Confusion Status Status Duration 5 sec S-11 P E Area of Effect Inner Radius 2 m Outer Radius 5 m Shockwave Radius 7 m AoE Duration 10 s Damage Damage Element Gas Inner Radius 3 Gas Inner Durable 3 Gas Outer Radius 2 - 0 Outer Durable 2 - 0 Penetration Direct Anti-Tank II AoE Effect Status Gas Status Strength 100 Second Status Gas_Confusion Status Strength 100 Demolition Force 30 Stagger Force 10 Push Force 10

The Speargun fires a projectile that can penetrate Tank I armor before embedding itself and releasing a cloud of gas similar in strength to a G-4 Gas Grenade but with a smaller radius that grows over time. The weapon is comparable to a RS-422 Railgun that has been set to Safe mode; however, a few quirks set it apart. The Speargun fires instantly, no charge-up required. However, it has significantly fewer reserves, a longer reload time, and much higher projectile drag. The spears can be shot at the ground to release gas and prevent the advancement of enemies much like G-4 Gas Grenades. The projectile and explosion both have a demolition force of 30, allowing it to destroy spawners such as Bug Holes, Fabricators and Grounded Warp Ships as well as PoI containers and Lightning Spires.

A single spear has extreme stagger force and can interrupt heavy enemies like Bile Titans from spewing or Chargers during a charge. The gas will also confuse the Charger and make dealing with it easier. If positioned correctly, two spear shots fired at a Charger's rear can cleave and hit its inner flesh. The multiplied damage to main will cause the Charger to bleed out and die; however. this works only on normal Chargers, Spore Chargers and Rupture Chargers but not Behemoths as Behemoths only have 50% to main on their rears, whereas the normal variants have 150%. The gas released from the spears can force Rupture strain Terminids to surface themselves from a distance. They will also be blinded by the gas, making them much more manageable. Much like the Railgun, a single spear can destroy a Hulk when shot directly at the eye. If the user misses the eye, Hulks will frequently be stunned by the gas allowing easy access to their heat sink, or a second attempt at shooting their eye. The Speargun excels at sealing Bug Holes compared to other options owing to the capability for the projectile to overpenetrate light to medium targets. In situations where a bug is emerging from the hole and could block other munitions from sealing it shut, the spear projectile can simply pass through the obstructed opening and detonate behind the enemy, sealing the hole on top of them.

The NEAT is a disposable cluster munition support weapon similar to the RL-77 Airburst Rocket Launcher which releases bomblets on impact. It exchanges bomblet damage for fire pools as well as fire and napalm damage over time. Unlike the RL-77, the NEAT's bomblets "bounce" off of surfaces, primarily walls or rocks. This makes the coverage area of the NEAT inconsistent, as its bomblets do not spread far when shot directly at the ground; the NEAT must often be shot at a surface to allow its bomblets to spread and cover a wider area. The NEAT is the first disposable horde clear support weapon. The NEAT is also the first disposable support weapon that uses napalm DoT (Heavy Burn) which makes it extremely deadly for area denial. The area denial provided is unmatched when used in tandem with support weapons such as the LAS-99 Quasar Cannon or APW-1 Anti-Materiel Rifle that cannot clear hordes. The NEAT can be compared to other crowd-clearing stratagems like the Orbital Gatling Barrage, Eagle Napalm Airstrike, or MD-8 Gas Mines. The NEAT boasts better range and response time so long as the user already has a NEAT on them before engaging an enemy group or reinforcement. However, the cooldown on the NEATs is significantly longer than other stratagems popular for this job. This, combined with the awkward nature of being sent two at once like typical EAT-17 Expendable Anti-Tanks, makes it more difficult for general usage. Despite not having an extending animation like the EAT-17, the NEAT still has the same readying delay.

The MS-11 Solo Silo is a unique expendable support weapon that fires a laser-guided missile with the same blast radius as the Eagle 500kg Bomb and EAT-411 Leveller but with greater damage and armor penetration. Able to engage targets anywhere on the map, provided line of sight is maintained, it is the highest damage support weapon and boasts greater armor penetration than any red stratagem at Anti-Tank V for direct impacts. Capable of taking out Factory Striders, Vox Engines and Bile Titans with one hit to the body, the Solo Silo's lethality is second only to the B-100 Portable Hellbomb. The Solo Silo releases a moderate blast around itself when fired, which can ragdoll fellow Helldivers. It is advised to keep a distance ≥15m from the silo when launching. The SH-32 Shield Generator Pack provides protection from the shockwave, allowing the diver to stay on target with the remote. The Solo Silo has a health value of 1,500 once embedded into the ground, and becomes unusable if destroyed. Enemies do not target the Solo Silo, so it is typically only destroyed via negligence. The Solo Silo's targeting system guides its missile in real time; by holding down fire key, the missile will actively follow the laser until it reaches its target or expends its 15 seconds of thruster fuel. If the player releases the trigger after firing the silo, whether voluntarily or from ragdoll, the Helldiver will immediately discard the laser pointer as it is rendered unusable even if the missile is still in flight. As a one-handed remote, the laser pointer can be used while carrying mission items (e.g., Intel Package). Just be aware that the Helldiver will also drop those items when the remote is dropped, something that’s easy to miss during a hot extraction and could lead to failing the mission. It can be used to dispatch moving targets, particularly aerial ones, such as the Leviathan or Dragonroach. However, due to the missile's relatively slow travel time and manual targeting, it is best to avoid using it against especially fast enemies, like Stingrays. The Solo Silo is capable of destroying Automaton Drop Ships and Illuminate Warp Ships before they deploy troops. The Solo Silo can destroy any enemy spawner, including Bile Titan Bug Holes and Bulk Fabricators, and additionally Enemy Bio-Processors, Command Bunkers, Illegal Broadcast Towers, Shrieker Nests, and Spore Spewers. The Solo Silo cannot take down Stratagem Jammers, Detector Towers, Illuminate Monoliths or Rogue Research Stations, as these structures require a demolition force of 50 to destroy (the silo has demo force of 40.)

The following Ship Modules affect the MS-11 Solo Silo: Department Ship Module Effect PatrioticAdministration Center Streamlined Request Process Decreases Support Weapon stratagem cooldown by 10%. General Call-in Time Standard 7.75 seconds Upgraded 4.75 seconds Uses Unlimited Cooldown Standard 480 seconds With Morale Augmentation 456 seconds

CQC-9 DEFOLIATION TOOL Recoil 6.25 Horizontal Recoil 2.5 Vertical Recoil 10 Spread ↔[10.00] ↕[10.00] Sway 1 Ergonomics 65 Noise No sound Stamina Cost 5% Attacks *CQC-9 DEFOLIATION TOOL_dm Damage CQC-9 DEFOLIATION TOOL_dm Damage Standard 450 Melee vs. Durable 225 Melee Penetration Direct Medium Slight Angle Medium Large Angle Medium Extreme Angle Unarmored Special Effects Status Stun Small Status Strength 5 Demolition Force 10 Stagger Force 10 Push Force 30

The Defoliation Tool increases armor penetration from Medium to Anti-Tank I as well as demolition force from 10 to 30 over the course of 0.5s of continuous contact with an enemy or structure at the rate of +2 AP and 20 demo force per second.

Defoliation Tool Specific[edit | edit source] The Defoliation Tool is unique among all melee weapons in that landing an attack on an enemy or destructible object will cause the sawblades to slowly drag along the target, rapidly dealing damage throughout the animation. Once the blades make contact with a target, the weapon will not disengage until the blades are no longer in contact with any target, even if the attack input is released. In the event the blades make contact with terrain such as the ground Helldivers will immediately disengage, resetting AP and demo accumulation. The damage is applied both per second (at multiple ticks per second), and per hit, meaning if you switch between body parts or move the saw in and out of the enemy quickly your DPS can be higher, however the blade needs to lose contact with the enemy for the ”swing damage” to reset. Switching between body parts or losing contact with the enemy will reset any AP and demo accumulation. [1] Foliage, low concrete barriers, heavy steel fences, Automaton Fabricators[2], Grounded Warp Ships[3], Landed Automaton Dropships and Lightning Spires can be destroyed via the Defoliation Tool. The range of the Defoliation Tool can be extended by diving, allowing it to damage and stun enemies further away. Moving the camera towards enemies while attacking will allow for more damage onto targets. It is advised to pair the Defoliation Tool with a backpack that either protects Helldivers, such as the SH-32 Shield Generator Pack, or one that allows for faster movement, such as the LIFT-850 Jump Pack and LIFT-182 Warp Pack. Due to the swing speed being just slow enough for stamina to start regenerating, this number is affected by Stamina Regen value and the Stamina Enhancement Booster. Additionally, hitting any targets will slow effective swing speed, further complicating this. Wearing Light armor with stamina enhancement booster, Helldivers can swing the Defoliation Tool a total of 34 times before stamina is completely drained. Wearing Heavy armor without the booster, Helldivers can swing the Defoliation Tool a total of 65+ times before stamina is completely drained. The Defoliation Tool's engine will not alert enemies to the Helldiver's presence while the weapon is being held or otherwise in use, unless swung in directly proximity to them. The Defoliation tool along with the CQC-20 Breaching Hammer are the only melee weapons that require both hands to use. Therefore, carriables like the Ballistic Shield or data drives will be stowed or dropped when these weapons are equipped. Melee Weapons[edit | edit source] Melee weapons deal all of their damage to the first segment or "body part" of any given entity that they come into contact with. Additional segments of the same unit that the weapon passes through will be ignored. This only applies to the swing damage of the chainsaw, and only long as it maintains contact with the enemy.[1] Wearing Armor with the Peak Physique or Rock Solid passive will increase melee damage by 40%, greatly increasing its lethality. Armor with the Reinforced Epaulettes passive will increase melee damage by 20%,. Attacking with the Defoliation Tool drains stamina. Holding the attack button will allow Helldivers to continuously thrust the Defoliation tool, even when stamina is empty.

rawSections.text: The M-1000 Maxigun is unlocked on the 3rd page of the Python Commandos Premium Warbond for 110 Medals.
General Call-in Time Standard 7.75 seconds Upgraded 4.75 seconds Uses Unlimited Cooldown Standard 480 seconds With Morale Augmentation 456 seconds

M-1000 MAXIGUN Fire Rate 1500 rpm Recoil 21.25 Horizontal Recoil 17.5 Vertical Recoil 25 Spread ↔[10.00] ↕[10.00] Sway 1 Ergonomics 4 Noise Medium (~48m) Capacity 1000 Rounds from Supply 500 Rounds from Ammo Box 250 Attacks *M-1000 P Projectile M-1000 P Projectile Mass 11 g Initial Velocity 920 m/s Drag Factor 30% Gravity Factor 100% Penetration Slowdown 25% Damage Standard 80 Ballistic vs. Durable 18 Ballistic Penetration Direct Medium Slight Angle Medium Large Angle Medium Extreme Angle Unarmored Special Effects Demolition Force 10 Stagger Force 15 Push Force 12

The M-1000 Maxigun boasts extremely high rate of fire and an ammunition reserve of 1000 rounds. As a backpack belt-fed weapon, it has the unique feature that it does not need to be manually reloaded like other backpack-reliant support weapons; however, it cannot be fired without its ammunition backpack equipped. The M-1000 Maxigun is also the first support weapon that "locks you down" to fire it, preventing you from moving but allowing you to rotate, elevate, and depress your weapon. When the M-1000 Maxigun and its Ammunition Backpack are initally picked up, a roughly 1-second animation will play where the Helldiver connects the ammunition feed chute into the Support Weapon. This connection will remain unless the two parts are forcibly detached, after which it must be reconnected in order to fire again.

Due to the Maxigun's extremely high rate of fire and by comparison relatively mediocre capacity, it is recommended to stay near ammo boxes, a Resupply,or a Helldiver carrying a B-1 Supply Pack. The Maxigun continuously feeds ammunition from its backpack, which means an ally supplying ammunition via the B-1 Supply Pack can keep the Maxigun continuously firing. Picking up an ammo box will restore 250 rounds directly to the backpack. The Maxigun has a brief 0.5s spin-up period before it begins to fire. This can be mitigated by spinning up while performing a dive. This also helps reduce recoil, due to the Helldiver now being prone. The Maxigun has extremely high recoil, so aiming down sights or going prone is recommended to reduce recoil. Additionally, a helldiver can use recoil-reducing Armor Passives such as Engineering Kit or Fortified. The Peak Physique passive significantly improves handling, allowing for extremely fast targeting. The passive also assists with minor recoil recovery and overall control. You cannot move at all while firing the Maxigun, but can still aim in any direction and transition between prone, crouching, and standing positions. As the Maxigun leaves you stationary during usage, it is advised to equip armor passives which reduce incoming damage like Fortified, as well as prone to take cover. Not only does this reduce the size of the Hellldiver's profile, but it reduces the high recoil of the Maxigun. The FX-12 Shield Generator Relay or G/SH-39 Shield can also be used to protect the user. It takes exactly 40 seconds of sustained fire with a full backpack to empty. The Maxigun excels at the destruction of many small to medium targets and delivering extremely high DPS on lightly armored weakpoints. The Maxigun's bullets cannot reliably penetrate corpses, so it is advised to keep a reasonable distance when fighting large hordes of bugs.

Entering and exiting any FRV type, the TD-220 Bastion MK XVI, any Exosuit, and any Emplacement stratagem will always make the Helldiver reattach the belt of the M-1000 Maxigun. The following bug also occurs every time the Helldiver leans out of any FRV and the Bastion's passenger seats.
