B/MD C4 PACK Main Health 10 Main Armor Unarmored Mags from Supply 1 Mags from Ammo Box 1 Max Rounds 1 Starting Rounds 1 Attacks *B/MD C4 PACK E Explosion B/MD C4 PACK E Area of Effect Inner Radius 3 m Outer Radius 7 m Shockwave Radius 8 m Damage Damage Element None Inner Radius 2000 Explosion Inner Durable 2000 Explosion Outer Radius 1999 - 0 Outer Durable 1999 - 0 Penetration Direct Anti-Tank III Slight Angle Anti-Tank III Large Angle Anti-Tank III Extreme Angle Anti-Tank III AoE Effect Demolition Force 40 Stagger Force 30 Push Force 40

The B/MD C4 Pack has two different components to it, the backpack and the detonator. The backpack stores up to 6 charges for the trigger and the trigger can hold a seventh to be thrown. The detonator has two different firing modes: Deploy Mode. This throws out a destructible C4 charge which will stick to the first surface it hits, which will be ignored by enemies. Detonate Mode. This will instantaneously trigger all currently deployed C4 charges to deliver a powerful explosion in a small radius.

C4 is a middle ground between dedicated Anti-Tank weaponry like the GR-8 Recoilless Rifle and explosive chaff clear weaponry like the GL-21 Grenade Launcher. As the C4 lacks a long or stationary reload, it is able to destroy multiple heavy units quicker than other AT weapons, and the explosion can be used to destroy swarms of chaff as well. In addition to the fast reload rate, C4 can also be thrown while running thanks to the one-handed trait. Because of this, C4 is very effective at fighting massive units like Bile Titans, Vox Engines and Hive Lords, as it can deal large damage very quickly while dodging attacks at the same time. It is highly recommended that Helldivers bind their "Quick Weapon Wheel Left" key in order to quickly switch between deploy and detonate mode with the C4. Helldivers can look at their right hand to see which mode they are in. In Deploy Mode they'll hold a C4 brick, in Detonate Mode they'll hold the detonator instead. A single C4 can be used to destroy spawners such as Bot Fabricators and shielded Grounded Warp Ships, even from the outside. C4 can also be used to destroy several Mission Objectives such as Command Bunkers, Bio-Processors, and Broadcast Towers. The C4 Pack can be used offensively against large enemies such as War Striders, Hulks, Charger Behemoths, and Harvesters, killing them with a single charge if placed correctly. The C4 is one of the best ways to kill Vox Engines, requiring only two from any angle without the need to hit weakpoints. Thrown C4 charges have a very generous throw range, but also benefit from the bonus throwing range of the Servo-Assisted and Desert Stormer armor passives. With quick timing, charges can be detonated in mid-air to 'airburst' them near vulnerable targets. There is a short delay when the trigger is pulled before C4 detonates. Pulling the trigger again will restart the delay, so avoid repeatedly tapping the trigger to ensure prompt detonation. The C4 pack is uniquely suited for stealth gameplay, allowing Helldivers to set explosives on enemy assets, then retreat to a safe distance before detonation. There is no limit to how many C4 charges may be deployed as long as the Helldiver can keep the backpack supplied.

When hosting a game, Helldivers may often experience a bug where thrown C4 bricks will alert any enemies they come in contact to. To alleviate this, the C4 carrier should designate another Helldiver as the host.

The following Ship Modules affect the B/MD C4 Pack: Department Ship Module Effect Patriotic Administration Center Streamlined Request Process Decreases Support Weapon stratagem cooldown by 10%. Superior Packing Methodology Resupply stratagem boxes refill Support Weapons with the maximum number of carriable magazines. Bridge Morale Augmentation Reduces cooldown time for all Stratagems by 5%. Engineering Bay Streamlined Launch Process All Support Weapons launch immediately once called in, reducing overall deployment time.

Breaching Hammer Specific[edit | edit source] The Breaching Hammer is a unique anti-tank support weapon capable of rapidly reloading from a relatively large ammunition pool without needing a backpack, at the cost of minuscule range due to being a melee weapon. It is most effective against heavy enemies with less health or easily reachable weak spots, such as Chargers, Hulks, Tanks, and War Striders, which can be destroyed in one or two hits with a charge attached. Special care should be taken when facing enemies with effective close quarters weapons or those which explode on death such as Shredder Tanks or Bile Spewers. The Anti-Tank II explosion of the Breaching Hammer's charge is not affected by Armor Passives that increase melee damage. Possessing a Demolition force of 30 with or without a charge, the Breaching Hammer may be used to open cargo containers or destroy foliage, low concrete barriers, heavy steel fences, Lightning Spires, Automaton Barbed Wire, Illegal Broadcast Towers, and Automaton statues. Automaton Fabricators, Grounded Warp Ships, and Landed Automaton Dropships can be destroyed only when a charge is attached. The explosion caused by the Breaching Hammer's charge injures all enemies in the blast radius, not just the main target. This can be used to counter crowds of melee enemies by crouching and attacking the floor before they get within their attack range. The explosion cannot damage the wielder or their SH-32 Shield Generator Pack. The Breaching Hammer, along with the Defoliation Tool, are the only melee weapons that require both hands to use. Mobility backpacks pair well with the Breaching Hammer, allowing the wielder to more easily get within melee range of priority targets. The LIFT-850 Jump Pack allows the most horizontal distance to be traveled at once, while granting enough height to hit the higher-up parts of larger enemies with a carefully-timed mid-jump swing. If attempting to hit enemies while mid-jump, aim to fly over or right beside the target so as to not crash directly into the target. Melee Weapons[edit | edit source] Melee weapons deal all of their damage to the first segment or "body part" of any given entity that they come into contact with. Additional segments of the same unit that the weapon passes through will be ignored. Wearing Armor with the Peak Physique or Rock Solid passive will increase melee damage by 40%, greatly increasing its lethality. Armor with the Reinforced Epaulettes passive will increase melee damage by 20%. Attacking with a melee weapon drains stamina. Holding the attack button will allow you to continuously attack, even when stamina is empty.

The following Ship Modules affect the CQC-20 Breaching Hammer: Department Ship Module Effect PatrioticAdministrationCenter Streamlined Request Process Decreases Support Weapon stratagem cooldown by 10%. Superior Packing Methodology Resupply stratagem boxes refill Support Weapons with the maximum number of carriable magazines. Payroll Management System Reduces reload time for all support weapons by 10%. Bridge Morale Augmentation Reduces cooldown time for all stratagems by 5%. EngineeringBay Streamlined Launch Process All Support Weapon stratagems launch immediately once called in, reducing overall deployment time.
The SH-32 Shield Generator Pack may block the explosion from hitting enemies.[1]

The Leveller is most comparable to the MS-11 Solo Silo. Both are high-power, single-use anti-tank support weapons with identical blast radius and demolition force. The Leveller is much quicker to deploy and has a 33% shorter cooldown, while the Solo Silo has greater power and range. Due to its immense damage and explosion radius, the EAT-411 Leveller can be used for both large crowds and Massive enemies like Bile Titans or Factory Striders. The Leveller's projectile shares the same drag and gravity characteristics of the GP-20 Ultimatum, but with significantly higher velocity at 50 m/s compared to only 20m/s. The projectile travels approximately 80m when fired straight up on flat terrain. Similar to the EAT-700 Expendable Napalm, the EAT-411 Leveller has a base cooldown of 140 seconds. However, only one launcher will be sent down per call-in. The weapon's 40 demo force allows it to destroy enemy spawners from the outside and close Bile Titan Bug Holes. This is not enough to destroy objects such as Stratagem Jammers or Detector Towers City walls and buildings can be destroyed. Grounded Warp Ships will be destroyed on a direct hit anywhere on their outer hull, even with the shields fully intact.

General Call-in Time Standard 7.75 seconds Upgraded 4.75 seconds Uses Unlimited Cooldown Standard 480 seconds With Morale Augmentation 456 seconds

GL-28 BELT-FED GRENADE LAUNCHER Fire Rate 320 rpm Recoil 23.75 Horizontal Recoil 17.5 Vertical Recoil 30 Spread ↔[4.00] ↕[4.00] Sway 1 Ergonomics 20 Noise Medium (~48m) Capacity 120 Attacks *GL-28 P Projectile **GL-28 P IE Explosion GL-28 P Projectile Mass 50 g Initial Velocity 100 m/s Drag Factor 120% Gravity Factor 100% Penetration Slowdown 25% Explosion On Impact GL-28_P_IE Damage Standard 0 Ballistic vs. Durable 0 Ballistic Penetration Direct Heavy Slight Angle Heavy Large Angle Heavy Extreme Angle Unarmored Special Effects Demolition Force 10 Stagger Force 30 Push Force 10 GL-28 P IE Area of Effect Inner Radius 2 m Outer Radius 4 m Shockwave Radius 5.5 m Damage Damage Element None Inner Radius 150 Explosion Inner Durable 150 Explosion Outer Radius 149 - 0 Outer Durable 149 - 0 Penetration Direct Heavy AoE Effect Demolition Force 30 Stagger Force 20 Push Force 20

The GL-28 boasts high rate of fire and an ammunition backpack with 120 grenades. As a backpack belt-fed weapon, it has the unique feature that it does not need to be manually reloaded like other backpack-reliant support weapons; however, it cannot be fired without its ammunition backpack equipped. Unlike the M-1000 Maxigun, Helldivers can move freely while firing the GL-28, allowing for greater flexibility. When the GL-28 Belt-Fed Grenade Launcher and its Ammunition Backpack are initally picked up, a roughly 1-second animation will play where the Helldiver connects the ammunition feed chute into the Support Weapon. This connection will remain unless the two parts are forcibly detached, in which it must be reconnected in order to fire again.

The GL-28 Belt-Fed Grenade Launcher is a high-capacity grenade launcher that excels at inflicting area damage against very large groups of small enemies while also being able to eliminate heavier targets thanks to its Heavy Armor Penetration. Compared to the standalone GL-21 Grenade Launcher, the GL-28 trades damage and blast radius for Heavy armor penetration, increased ammo count and rate of fire. The GL-28 has better ammo economy and higher uptime vs. the GL-21 due to having a single long belt of 120 grenades vs having to reload 10-round belts. The GL-28 has two higher rpm options (240 & 320) as well as significantly lower recoil and spread than the GL-21, allowing for much more accurate shots and making it ideal for horde-clearing and stagger-locking fast enemies such as Stalkers and charging Alpha Commanders. Attacking heavy enemies with the GL-28 set to its maximum rate of fire is a relatively quick way to destroy them short of anti-tank weapons, but without assistance will take many dozens of grenades to accomplish against massive enemies like Bile Titans. Grenades fired from the GL-28 have a 4m arming distance that prevents them from exploding too soon after firing, causing them to harmlessly bounce off objects and enemies at very close range. However, after ricocheting, the grenade can still explode once it travels beyond this safety range and strikes the ground, nearby objects, or enemies. Like other explosive weapons, the GL-28 can destroy Bug Holes and Automaton Fabricators by shooting into their apertures. This is especially useful on high-difficulty Terminid missions, as there can sometimes be upwards of 50 Bug Holes in total. The GL-28 has the same issue as the M-1000 Maxigun where leaning out of the FRV (Fast Recon Vehicle) removes the belt from the grenade launcher forcing the Helldiver to re-attach it. When firing the GL-28 behind low cover, its grenades can hit the cover in front of its user due to the weapon being hip-fired. Aiming in first person will make the projectiles come from the center of the camera, making firing from cover easier.

Entering and exiting any FRV type, the TD-220 Bastion MK XVI, any Exosuit, and any Emplacement stratagem will always make the Helldiver reattach the belt of the GL-28 Belt-Fed Grenade Launcher. The following bug also occurs every time the Helldiver leans out of any FRV and the Bastion's passenger seats.

EngineeringBay Streamlined Launch Process All Support Weapon stratagems launch immediately once called in, reducing overall deployment time.

The B/FLAM-80 Cremator boasts increased fire damage and an ammunition backpack with 500 units of fuel. As a backpack hose-fed weapon, it has the unique feature that it does not need to be manually reloaded like other backpack-reliant support weapons; however, it cannot be fired without its ammunition backpack equipped. Unlike the M-1000 Maxigun, Helldivers can move freely while firing the B/FLAM-80 Cremator, allowing for greater flexibility. When the B/FLAM-80 Cremator and its Ammunition Backpack are initally picked up, a roughly 1-second animation will play where the Helldiver connects the fuel hose into the Support Weapon. This connection will remain unless the two parts are forcibly detached, in which it must be reconnected in order to fire again.

The B/FLAM-80 Cremator is a more powerful FLAM-40 Flamethrower. It has increased range and coverage, deals more damage due to its double-barreled nature, and can fire for longer periods of time. However, it requires its associated backpack tank to operate and has less fuel time overall than a fully resupplied FLAM-40. The Cremator has a range of roughly 25 meters (measured in first person), which is 25% more than the FLAM-40's 20-meter range. Before firing, the pilot light must be ignited by holding the fire button. It may be fired instantly at any time while the pilot light is active. The pilot light will extinguish automatically after a roughly 12-second period of disuse. The pilot light will appear to visually extinguish roughly 2 seconds before it mechanically extinguishes. Firing at the floor will create a pool of fire that continues to burn for several seconds. This can set Helldivers on fire too, so advancing whilst firing is not advised. Diving directly backwards while shooting the Cremator will catch the Helldiver on fire, due to their legs passing in front of the jet. While the weapon is fired from slightly different locations between first- and third-person views, both can still easily light a Helldiver's legs on fire. Its fire jet deals continuous damage throughout its travel. Skewering a target lengthwise can greatly increase the effect. This weapon performs best on open ground. The flames are easily blocked by terrain or worse, bounced back at the Helldiver at short range. Each full backpack contains enough fuel to fire for 62.35 seconds, and fuel is not consumed between lighting the pilot light and firing.

Entering and exiting any FRV type, the TD-220 Bastion MK XVI, any Exosuit, and any Emplacement stratagem will always make the Helldiver reattach the hose of the B/FLAM-80 Cremator. The following bug also occurs every time the Helldiver leans out of any FRV and the Bastion's passenger seats.

General Call-in Time Standard 6.75 seconds Upgraded 3.75 seconds Uses Unlimited Cooldown Standard 70 seconds With Morale Augmentation 66.5 seconds

MGX-42 BULLET STORM Fire Rate 1300 rpm Recoil 6.75 Horizontal Recoil 4.5 Vertical Recoil 9 Spread ↔[5.00] ↕[5.00] Sway 1 Ergonomics 25 Noise Medium (~48m) Capacity 300 Spare Magazines 0 Starting Magazines 0 Mags from Supply 0 Mags from Ammo Box 1 Barrels x 24 Attacks *MGX-42 P Projectile MGX-42 P Projectile Mass 4.5 g Initial Velocity 450 m/s Drag Factor 60% Gravity Factor 100% Penetration Slowdown 25% Damage Standard 100 Ballistic vs. Durable 25 Ballistic Penetration Direct Light Slight Angle Light Large Angle Light Extreme Angle Unarmored Special Effects Demolition Force 10 Stagger Force 20 Push Force 10

Due to its low cooldown, two uses per call-in, expendable nature, and large ammunition load, the Bullet Storm is extremely flexible as a support weapon. The Bullet Storm boasts an extremely high fire rate of 1300rpm, comparatively low recoil, and an impressive 100 damage per shot, higher than its counterparts, the MG-43 Machine Gun and the M-105 Stalwart. This makes it particularly effective against the Illuminate and Terminids, given the abundance of lightly armored, high health targets. It is not especially effective against the Automatons due to their propensity to engage at range, their armor, and their small weakpoints that require precise aiming, something the Bullet Storm is not especially good at. The high rate of fire means the Bullet Storm expends its 300 round capacity in ~14 seconds of continuous firing. It is recommended to only use sustained fire against groups of enemies and large unarmored targets to save ammunition. The low recoil makes the Bullet Storm relatively accurate even in sustained fire or while moving, especially in first person view. The Bullet Storm can be used as a supplement to a slower, Anti-Tank Support Weapon, being called down upon encountering hordes of targets, such as during a Bug Breach. When calling down the Bullet Storm against hordes, "reloading" is as quick as picking up the second gun from the Hellpod. If used in tandem with the EAT-17 Expendable Anti-Tank, Helldivers can call in 600 bullets and two anti-tank projectiles every 70 seconds, even without any Ship Upgrades. The Bullet Storm has poor bullet drag and velocity for a machine gun, and no reticle or sight in first person view. It is less effective at longer range and difficult to aim precisely at individual targets and weakpoints. The Bullet Storm can easily be aimed using its tracer bullets, but the weapon's ergonomics, though better than most machine guns, hamper the ability to adjust aim against distant targets. In first person view, the Bullet Storm's muzzle flash can make it difficult to see distant enemies and bullet impacts. The Bullet Storm’s quick cooldown means it is almost always available upon reinforcement of additional Helldivers. Even if a fresh Helldiver is called in far from their equipment, in a matter of seconds they can have another Bullet Storm at hand. Because Bullet Storms arrive in pairs, they can be easily distributed to teammates who might need a support weapon. The Bullet Storm’s quick cooldown also allows the Hellpod itself to be used as a weapon, dealing 2500 Anti-Tank VI damage upon impact.

The following Ship Modules affect the MGX-42 Bullet Storm: Department Ship Module Effect Patriotic Administration Center Streamlined Request Process Decreases Support Weapon stratagem cooldown by 10%. Bridge Morale Augmentation Reduces cooldown time for all Stratagems by 5%. EngineeringBay Streamlined Launch Process All Support Weapon stratagems launch immediately once called in, reducing overall deployment time.

MGX-42 Bullet Storm's muzzle flash is not aligned with the weapon and always points to the north. The Meltagun fires a continuous beam like the LAS-98 Laser Cannon but trades range and unlimited ammo for massive DPS and higher armor penetration. However, unlike other beam-firing laser weapons, the Meltagun does not set enemies on fire. The Meltagun has a short charge-up time before firing, leaving a short window of vulnerability for users. To effectively fire it, Helldivers should maintain some distance between enemies in order to charge up the weapon and land shots. Once the Meltagun is charged, it fires continuously for roughly 1.4 seconds before needing to be charged again, dealing a maximum theoretical damage of 3,640 per burst. The Meltagun, however, suffers from damage fall-off, which is unique for beam weapons. 40% of damage is lost at its maximum range of 15 meters — dealing ~1,560 DPS. With 3 rounds per magazine and 4 spares, the Meltagun can be fired 15 times before running empty. This can be alleviated by equipping armor with the Siege-Ready passive, adding one more spare magazine. The Meltagun is extremely effective against heavy enemies such as Annihilator Tanks, Chargers, and Fleshmobs, killing them in 1 to 2 shots anywhere on their body. Massive enemies can be destroyed with 1 to 2 shots to their weak spots, such as a Factory Strider's belly panels and a Bile Titan's head. The Meltagun is also extremely effective against a variety of enemy structures such as Shrieker Nests, Spore Spewers, and Command Bunkers, destroying them all in one shot. All enemy spawners (besides Bug Holes) can be destroyed with 1 to 2 bursts of the Meltagun. Grounded Warp Ships will require 3 bursts if the energy shield is deployed, one burst being used to take down the shield.
